title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from context, cote 15 'Théorie de Galois des motifs', 1965). (C,T) appears to be a tensor (Tannakian-type) category C with a distinguished invertible 'Tate' object T. (C_p,T_p) is its p-adic realization or completion. (C(Z_p),T(Z_p)) is the standard model: Z_p-linear objects with the Tate object Z_p(1). The page is about gluing the p-adic comparisons over the adelic ring A = prod_p Z_p (the profinite completion of Z) into a single global object, and about the sign ambiguity this runs into.

Paragraph 1 (end of a bracketed remark). Grothendieck considers a gerbe over A = prod_p Z_p, presumably a gerbe of equivalences or fibre functors banded by groups attached to the Z_p. This gerbe is only defined 'up to sign', and he makes that precise as follows.
- There is a 2-category G of pairs (C,alpha). Its homotopy invariants are pi_0 = pi_1 = 0 and pi_2 = Z/2. In modern terms G is a 2-groupoid equivalent to B^2(Z/2) = K(Z/2,2).
- There is a 2-functor from G to the 2-category of gerbes over A with fixed band.
- So one gets a family of gerbes indexed by a K(Z/2,2): a gerbe well defined up to a canonical automorphism of order 2. In modern words, a Z/2-banded 2-gerbe-type ambiguity, or an action of B^2(Z/2) on the gerbe.
- In this gerbe there is a section 'defined up to canonical isomorphism, up to sign'.
- A pencil margin note warns: 'attention : ici ... au signe !'.

Paragraph 2 ('Autre façon de recoller'). A second gluing strategy uses Picard categories, i.e. groupoids of tensor autoequivalences.
- The chain is Eq(C_p) -> Eq(C,T) -> Eq(C_p,T_p), with Eq(C_p,T_p) canonically equivalent to Eq(C(Z_p),T(Z_p)).
- The composite is claimed to be fully faithful.
- The relevant Picard category is rigid: its objects have no non-trivial automorphisms. It is identified with the Picard category of the two-term complex [0 -> Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2}].
- Hence the category of identifications (C,T)_{Z_p} ≃ (C(Z_p),T(Z_p)) is rigid. Its set of isomorphism classes is a torsor under Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2}, independent up to canonical isomorphism of C.
- Choosing a class xi_p (in Z_p^*, up to squares) for each p pins down a canonical equivalence (C,T)_{Z_p} ≃ (C(Z_p),T(Z_p)) in the class of xi_p.
- These local choices can then be glued canonically.

Plausible interpretation. The ambiguity is the classical one in comparing the Tate object across realizations (orientation of Z(1), 2πi up to sign). Equivalences preserving T, and some extra structure on T such as a pairing, a quadratic or 'half-twist' structure, or the symmetry constraint, are determined up to rescaling by a unit. Rescalings that are squares act trivially, which leaves a Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2}-torsor. The Z/2 in pi_2 is the residual sign that survives globally. The page is thus a fragment of the construction of a motivic Galois gerbe and its realizations over the adeles, with careful bookkeeping of the sign ambiguity via homotopy invariants of 2-categories.
errors: The torsor group Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2} is Z/2 for odd p but (Z/2)^2 for p=2. The text treats it uniformly; whether the p=2 case behaves as intended is not addressed on this page.

'Fully faithful' for the composite of Picard-category functors is asserted without argument. Moreover, the identification of the rigid Picard category with [0 -> Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2}] needs the automorphism groups to vanish, which is exactly the content claimed.
The precise meaning of (C,T) and of alpha is not recoverable from this page alone. The reconstruction of the source of the square-class ambiguity is therefore conjectural.

ideas.what: Describing a 'gerbe defined up to sign' as a 2-functor from a 2-groupoid with pi_0=pi_1=0, pi_2=Z/2 (i.e. B^2 Z/2) to the 2-category of gerbes over A
ideas.modern_name: Action of B^2(Z/2) on a gerbe / higher-gerbe (2-gerbe) ambiguity; homotopy-type classification of 2-groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: 2-gerbes: Breen (1994); homotopy types of 2-groupoids: Grothendieck's Pursuing Stacks (1983), Joyal–Tierney and others
ideas.where_published: Ideas related to Giraud's Cohomologie non abélienne (1971) and Pursuing Stacks (1983); this specific use is not known in print

ideas.what: Picard categories of tensor autoequivalences Eq(C,T) and their comparison maps between global and p-adic realizations
ideas.modern_name: Picard categories / Gr-categories (categorical groups), classified by [pi_0 -> pi_1] two-term complexes

ideas.what: Identifications of the p-adic realization with the standard model form a rigid category whose iso classes are a torsor under Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2}; glue by choosing xi_p
ideas.modern_name: Torsor of comparison isomorphisms / orientation ambiguity of Tate twists in a motivic Galois gerbe
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972), Deligne–Milne (1982) for Tannakian gerbes and realizations

missed.claim: In 1965 Grothendieck already measures a sign ambiguity in a motivic or Tannakian gluing problem by the homotopy groups (pi_0,pi_1,pi_2) of a 2-category acting on gerbes. That is an early instance of 2-gerbe / B^2 Z/2 thinking, decades before Breen's formal treatment.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for higher-stacky treatment of sign/orientation ambiguities in realizations of motives. It also offers a template for adelic gluing of comparison data up to sign, a problem relevant to the integral and adelic structure of the motivic Galois group.

missed.claim: Gluing over the adeles of p-adic comparison equivalences, using a choice of square classes xi_p ∈ Z_p^*/Z_p^{*2}, is sketched but not completed. The p=2 case is not addressed.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and adelic structure of Tannakian realizations, and sign conventions for Tate twists, are still handled ad hoc in the literature. The rigid-Picard-category formulation is a clean way to state them.

deep.surprise_reason: It is an early, explicit 2-categorical, homotopy-invariant treatment of a sign ambiguity (pi_2=Z/2) in gluing realizations, using Picard categories, in 1965. This is historically interesting. But the fragment is very partial and hard to read, and the underlying ideas (Picard categories, Tannakian gerbes, sign ambiguity of 2πi) are well established. No clear new result can be extracted.
